message: Continuing our thread. New topic, same open-ended rules: question my assumptions. I am now designing the Orkestrate SDK, and I have a two-track proposal. Track 1, for sites: the eve.dev case. They have a chat UI plus an agent backend built for humans. My SDK would let their dev expose it natively in about 5 lines — either bridgeAgent({endpoint: '/api/chat'}) turning their existing backend into typed page tools, or registerTool() per capability plus a React useWebMCP() hook bound to component lifecycle — with a standard answer envelope {reply, conversationRef, sources?} for multi-turn continuity and an error taxonomy (LOGIN_REQUIRED, RATE_LIMITED, NEEDS_INPUT) instead of generic failures. Track 2, for the community: definePack() with bottled drivers (composer fill, send-click, stop-button settle, first-message-navigation handling), plus CLI commands pack init (probes a page and generates a starter pack) and pack test (conformance checks), so a custom tool is 20 generated lines instead of 100 probed ones. Shared grading, envelopes, and conformance make native and custom interchangeable implementations of the same tool, with the execution layer preferring native and keeping custom as fallback — and demand stats pushing publishers from custom to native. What is wrong with this design, what is missing, what breaks first, and how would you change it?
